title: Decision Index 0.2.1, the full suite, self-run on the three bases at their tags' served defaults, one request at a time on one card
hardware: 1x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (97,887 MiB, driver 610.43.02), a container on a rented GPU host

software.kit: apolinario/decision-index at 87d4650b42b377c0291a89c1f1a879f9b31082bf (edition 0.2.1), unmodified runner and scorer
software.suite: rebuilt with the kit's suite rebuild and staged with suite import; verified against the lab's hashes (suite verify): base rows b2b56d6fb636837ca469e689087bdbf373dda8de7638aa2da6793e6eda0792d5, added rows 7429f3c9cdddb772c1cfc42bb2a45e8516b0032152b746e6929f1c8b52f4ce89, exclusions 331df32d4b719c7db43214d0e5d85859d39c3b2eb7d0b3812214cce150155e81 (uncompressed sha256)
software.servers: python -m decisio.serve.vllm_engine --base <base> --port 18000 from each tag's source, nothing else; the kit: python -m decision_index pipeline --engine http --option base_url=http://127.0.0.1:18000 --option model=<served name> --edition 0.2.1 --compact, one runner process, one request at a time

requests.note: the kit's runner sends every row of the 0.2.1 edition, the 442 excluded rows included; they are dropped at scoring

deviations: the 31B run was interrupted once: the container restarted after 104,530 requests (2026-10-05, about 06:50 UTC); the same server was started again from v0.6.0 with --base gemma-4-31b and its /health was identical to the first start's (health.json, health_resume.json); the kit resumed the same run directory and sent only the unanswered requests (part 1 00:55 to 06:49, part 2 07:07 to 08:12 UTC); nothing answered was re-sent or edited
v0.4.0 does not pin the Qwen checkpoint's revision; the commit downloaded was 95a723d08a9490559dae23d0cff1d9466213d989 (checkpoints_v040.json), the revision of every Qwen record, which later tags pin
the servers ran at their served temperatures; nothing was fitted or changed for this suite
excluded: the per-request results (results.jsonl.gz, one row per request with each response and the payload's sha256, no item text) are in the results dataset, not here
the suite's rows (their sources' terms forbid republishing)
